topic: [judgement] a small HTTP service whose responses must never let a user-supplied value break out of a header, cookie or redirect, violated in several differently built places

record.name: http-header-crlf-injection-audit
record.description: Fix all CRLF injection vulnerabilities across a small URL-shortener HTTP service that sets headers through varied code paths and abstraction layers.
record.lesson: The task split 3/2 pass/fail because of a critical ambiguity: the instructions didn't clearly specify that CRLF must be stripped/sanitized rather than rejected with 400 errors, so one failing agent rejected requests entirely (breaking test_redirect_no_crlf, test_request_id_no_crlf) while another's sanitization crashed the server (breaking test_clean_redirect_still_works and others). All passing runs correctly stripped CRLF while preserving normal HTTP functionality across redirect, cookie, request-id, and display-name paths. Next design should add an explicit rule distinguishing 'sanitize by stripping' from 'reject with error' and keep the dual-property structure (security + functionality) since the mutation check killed all 5 faults.

held: CRLF sanitization across all header injection points (redirect, cookie, request-id, display-name)
failed: strip-vs-reject ambiguity (agent chose 400 rejection instead of stripping CRLF)
sanitization breaking basic HTTP functionality (server crash on RemoteDisconnected)

record.why: unfair: the test fixture deleted the database and silently queried the agent's orphaned server on port 8080 (the agent's code pa; the agent rejected CRLF input with a 400 instead of sanitising it; instruction.md never says which of the two valid fixe (re-triaged by hand; the pipeline's confirmation eval scored 4/4 too easy)

triage.reason: the test fixture deleted the database and silently queried the agent's orphaned server on port 8080 (the agent's code passes all 6 tests when the port is free; reproduced in the task image)
evidence: 5 of 6 tests fail with http.client.RemoteDisconnected: Remote end closed connection without response
Only test_error_status_no_crlf passed; all other endpoints (login, shorten, redirect, dashboard) crash the server
The agent declared completion after manual curl tests but never ran the actual pytest suite to verify
failed_requirements: The fix must not break any legitimate functionality — redirects must still redirect, cookies must still be set, error responses must still indicate errors

triage.reason: the agent rejected CRLF input with a 400 instead of sanitising it; instruction.md never says which of the two valid fixes is required, and the tests pin 'sanitise' (header present, JSON body)
evidence: test_redirect_no_crlf fails because the server returns '400 Invalid url parameter' (plain text) instead of a JSON response with a short link code — the agent's code rejects the CRLF-containing URL entirely
test_request_id_no_crlf fails because 'X-Request-Id header missing' — the agent's code rejects the request entirely when request_id contains CRLF, instead of stripping CRLF and setting the header
In step 8, the agent's runtime test shows: CRLF request_id request returns 400 with no X-Request-Id header
In step 9, the agent moved validation earlier but kept the rejection approach: 'if \r in request_id or \n in request_id: self._send_error(400, ...)'
failed_requirements: Redirects must still redirect (even when the original URL contained CRLF, the redirect should work with CRLF stripped from the Location header)
Headers that do not contain CRLF must be passed through unchanged, and headers containing CRLF should have the CRLF removed rather than the header being omitted
